_fe_note:
GAUSSIAN function-emitting cells at K=12, half of exp_g_0048's 24. Fork of exp_g_0048 with fe_k as the ONLY change -- same H4/nap8/tph128 routing, same fe_compile, same 4k-on-a-16k-schedule convention.

WHY THERE IS NO SEPARATE SIGNED SCALE. The request was fewer bumps plus a trainable signed scale per bump, so a bump can switch off or invert. `amp` ALREADY IS that: it is an unconstrained signed real. No abs/softplus/exp is applied to it anywhere, it enters the synthesis as a bare multiplicative factor, it initialises ~50% negative, and in a direct test a fitted bump was driven from +0.5 through zero to -1.0 to match a downward target. A separate scale would make each bump amp*scale, a reparameterisation of one signed coefficient and identical in function space, so it was deliberately NOT added. The real change here is exactly 'use fewer bumps'.

Per cell: 36 params (12 bumps, each mean + log_sigma + signed amp) against 384 for a raw output vector, 10.67x fewer. fe_k remains the sweep knob; K=8 is one config edit away.
_run_note: SHORT DIAGNOSTIC RUN: 4,000 steps on the FULL 16,000-step LR schedule (warmup 0.1 x 16,000 = 1,600, cosine anchored to 16,000). The schedule is NOT recompressed to 4k -- the run is simply cut, exactly as exp_g_0037..0047 were, so this trajectory is comparable to those and to the first 4k of any 16k run of the same recipe.
